rightToWorkByNationality._comment: ISO 3166 alpha-2 nationality -> countries where that passport already allows work. Users can also declare a visa/PR they hold.

move: Your employer must hold a UK sponsor licence. They give you a Certificate of Sponsorship for the job.
The job must be an eligible occupation and pay at least the visa salary bar, or the job's going rate if that is higher.
You apply online and give fingerprints at a visa centre in India. Decisions usually take about 3 weeks.
You pay the visa fee and the Immigration Health Surcharge, unless your employer covers them.
Your partner and children can come with you as dependants.
The job usually needs to be on Ireland's Critical Skills Occupations List, with an offer of at least 2 years.
Your employer or you apply for the permit online before you travel. Current processing times are published by the Department of Enterprise.
Once the permit is granted, you apply for an Irish entry visa in India.
Your spouse or partner can join you straight away and work.
After 2 years you can usually move to Stamp 4 and work for any employer.
No sponsor licence is needed: any German employer can hire you if the salary meets the Blue Card threshold (lower for shortage jobs such as IT).
You need a degree recognised in Germany (check the anabin database). Experienced IT specialists can qualify without one.
You apply for a national visa at the German mission in India (through VFS), then get the Blue Card in Germany.
Your family can join you, and your spouse can work.
Permanent residence is possible after about 27 months, or sooner with German at B1 level.
Your employer must be a recognised sponsor with the IND. They apply for you.
The salary must meet the highly skilled migrant threshold for your age.
The IND usually decides within a few weeks. You then collect an entry visa (MVV) in India if you need one.
Your partner and children can come with you, and your partner can work.
You may qualify for the Dutch expat tax break (the 30% ruling).
Your employer applies for a work permit for you, or you qualify for an EU Blue Card with a degree and a high enough salary.
With the permit, you apply for a national (D) work visa at the Polish consulate in India.
Permits can take a few months, so ask your employer to start early.
Your family can join you through family reunification once you are settled.
Your employer applies for the Employment Pass online for you.
You need to pass the COMPASS points test and earn at least the qualifying salary, which rises with age.
Most applications are decided within a few weeks.
If you earn enough, your family can join you on Dependant's Passes.
Most job offers need a Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA). Tech roles through the Global Talent Stream are usually processed in about 2 weeks.
You then apply for a work permit and give biometrics at a visa centre in India.
Express Entry can give permanent residence without a job offer, so it is worth checking your points.
Your spouse can often get an open work permit.
Your employer must be an approved sponsor and nominate you for the role.
The salary must meet the income threshold for the visa stream.
You usually need at least 1 year of relevant experience and an English test result.
Your family can be included, and there is a path to permanent residence with your employer.

US.warning: H-1B needs the March lottery and the $100,000 fee for applicants abroad is in court. Off by default; most people from India reach the US through an internal L-1 transfer.
move: H-1B: your employer registers you in the lottery each March. If you are selected, you can start work from 1 October.
A $100,000 fee for applicants abroad is being challenged in court, so check the latest before you plan around it.
Many people from India move instead through an internal L-1 transfer after a year with a US company's team in India.
An H-4 spouse can work only in some cases.

jobTextRules._comment: Case-insensitive. A NEGATIVE match hides the job from anyone who needs a visa for that country, even at a sponsoring company.
negative: must have the right to work
must already have the right to work
must be eligible to work in
